stem: A flat loop is in a uniform magnetic field B. The angle θ is measured between B and the normal to the plane of the loop. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?
explanation: Magnetic flux through a planar area is Φ = BA cos θ when θ is measured to the surface normal.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A rectangular loop of area 0.040 m² has its normal at 60° to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.30 T. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

stem: What change is necessary for an emf to be induced around a stationary, closed conducting loop?
options: The loop must always be moving
The loop must have non-zero resistance
The magnetic flux through the loop must change with time
The magnetic field must be non-zero but constant
explanation: An induced emf requires a time-varying magnetic flux linkage; steady non-zero flux alone does not induce emf.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A coil of 80 turns experiences a uniform change in flux per turn from 0.030 Wb to 0.0050 Wb in 0.20 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A circular conducting loop lies in the page. A uniform magnetic field directed into the page increases in strength, as shown. What is the direction of the induced conventional current in the loop?
options: No current because the loop is stationary
explanation: The increasing inward flux is opposed by a field out of the page. By the right-hand grip rule, this requires anticlockwise current.
diagramAlt: Circular conducting loop with increasing magnetic field into the page.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A rectangular loop moves at constant speed into a region where a uniform magnetic field points into the page, as shown. As the loop enters, what is the direction of its induced current?
options: There is no induced current until the whole loop is inside
explanation: Flux into the page increases as the loop enters, so the induced current makes a field out of the page: anticlockwise.
diagramAlt: Rectangular loop partly entering a magnetic field directed into the page.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A straight conducting rod of length L moves at speed v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B, with the rod perpendicular to v. Which expression gives the magnitude of the motional emf across the rod?
explanation: For this perpendicular geometry the motional emf is ε = BvL.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A vertical conducting rod of length 0.30 m moves horizontally at 4.0 m s⁻¹ through a magnetic field of 0.50 T into the page, as shown. What is the induced emf magnitude between its ends?
diagramAlt: A vertical rod moving to the right through a uniform field into the page.

stem: A metal rod moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. Its speed is gradually doubled while its length and the field remain unchanged. What happens to the magnitude of the motional emf?
options: It becomes four times as large
explanation: Motional emf is proportional to speed: ε = BvL.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A rectangular coil of 50 turns has width 0.12 m across its leading edge. It moves at 3.0 m s⁻¹ into a uniform 0.40 T magnetic field, with the edge perpendicular to the direction of motion, as shown. What is the induced emf magnitude while the coil is only partly inside?
explanation: Rate of area swept out per turn is Lv. Thus |ε| = NBLv = (50)(0.40)(0.12)(3.0) = 7.2 V.
diagramAlt: Rectangular coil translating into a uniform magnetic field region.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A rectangular coil moves entirely inside a large region of uniform magnetic field. Its orientation, area and speed remain constant. What emf is induced in the complete coil?
options: A constant emf proportional to its speed
An emf increasing with distance travelled
explanation: The flux through the coil remains constant while it is fully inside the uniform region; total induced emf is zero.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A rectangular coil rotates steadily about an axis perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The angle θ is between the plane of the coil and the field direction. When is the magnitude of induced emf maximum?
explanation: Flux is BA sin θ for plane-to-field angle θ. The magnitude of the induced emf is proportional to |cos θ| and is greatest when the plane is parallel to B.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A coil rotates at constant angular speed in a uniform magnetic field. Which statement correctly describes the induced emf?
options: It is sinusoidal and reverses sign every half-turn
It is zero if the coil has more than one turn
explanation: The flux linkage varies sinusoidally in time, so its time derivative—and hence the emf—is sinusoidal, alternating in sign every half rotation.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: The frequency of rotation of an ideal generator coil is doubled, while its magnetic field, area and turns remain unchanged. How do the peak emf and frequency of the emf change?
options: Peak emf stays constant; frequency doubles
Peak emf doubles; frequency stays constant
explanation: Peak emf is NBAω, so it doubles with angular frequency; the sinusoidal emf frequency also doubles.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A 150-turn coil has area 0.020 m² and rotates at 20 revolutions per second in a uniform magnetic field of 0.40 T. What is its peak induced emf?
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A generator coil rotates about an axis parallel to a uniform magnetic field. Its shape and orientation relative to that field do not change during rotation. What is the induced emf?
options: It is sinusoidal with a non-zero maximum
explanation: Rotation about the field axis leaves the component of area along B unchanged; flux is constant and induced emf is zero.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: Two separate coils are wound on the same iron core. The first coil is connected to a steady DC supply and the second to a sensitive ammeter. What is the current in the second coil after the first coil has been connected for a long time?
options: A constant current in one direction
explanation: Once current in the primary becomes steady, the magnetic flux through the secondary is constant, so no emf is induced.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: The primary current in a transformer-like arrangement is switched off rapidly. What happens in a nearby closed secondary coil?
options: A transient induced current appears while the magnetic flux changes
A current appears only if the primary remains on
A permanent DC current flows in the secondary
There is no induction because the coils do not touch
explanation: The rapid drop in primary current changes the flux linked with the secondary, producing a transient induced emf and current.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: Why can a large induced emf appear across a coil when its current is interrupted suddenly?
options: The coil changes the charge on every electron
The coil always creates a constant emf from its resistance
Induction occurs only when the coil moves
The coil creates an emf opposing the change in its own magnetic flux
explanation: A rapid current change produces a rapid change of flux linked with the same coil. Self-induction opposes the current change; no RL calculation is required.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: The graph shows flux per turn in a 20-turn coil versus time. During which interval is the induced emf magnitude greatest?
options: The emf is equal in all three intervals
explanation: |ε| = N|dΦ/dt|. From 0–2 s, |slope|=0.24/2=0.12 Wb s⁻¹, larger than 0 and 0.24/3=0.08 Wb s⁻¹.
diagramAlt: Flux per turn rises to 0.24 Wb by 2 seconds, remains constant until 5 seconds, then falls to zero at 8 seconds.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: The 20-turn coil in the flux–time graph has a resistance of 4.0 Ω. What is the magnitude of its induced current during the interval 5–8 s?
explanation: During 5–8 s the flux per turn changes by 0.24 Wb over 3.0 s. |ε| = 20(0.24/3.0)=1.6 V; I=1.6/4.0=0.40 A.
diagramAlt: Flux versus time for a 20-turn coil with a falling final segment.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A 40-turn coil undergoes the same change in flux per turn as a 20-turn coil during an equal time. What is the ratio of the magnitude of their induced emfs (40-turn to 20-turn)?
explanation: Faraday’s law gives |ε| ∝ N for a fixed rate of flux change: ratio 40/20 = 2.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A coil of 120 turns and area 0.015 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field which reverses uniformly from +0.20 T to −0.20 T in 0.060 s. What average emf magnitude is induced?

stem: A conducting bar is pulled at constant speed along horizontal conducting rails through a perpendicular magnetic field. The rails form a closed circuit with a resistor. Why is an external pulling force required?
options: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion
The resistor produces an electric force that drives the bar forwards
The magnetic flux must be conserved exactly
A constant bar speed requires continuously increasing kinetic energy
explanation: The induced current experiences a magnetic force opposing the motion. The external force supplies energy that becomes thermal energy in the resistor.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.

stem: A bar magnet is dropped through a horizontal closed conducting ring with its north pole pointing downward. Ignoring air resistance, what is true of the magnetic force from the induced ring current while the magnet approaches and while it moves away?
options: It accelerates the magnet in both stages
It opposes the motion in both stages
It always acts downward in both stages
It vanishes as long as the magnet is moving
explanation: As the magnet approaches or recedes, flux changes and Lenz’s law produces a magnetic force opposing that change and the motion, transferring mechanical energy to electrical/thermal energy.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 D.4 syllabus; supplied exam questions are difficulty benchmarks only.
